coordinates.object_orientation: Head -Y, tail +Y, dorsal +Z. Preserve fixed camera conventions.

concept.reason: Real scaled fossil and primary morphology descriptions plus museum whole-body comparator suffice; no generated concept image.

scope: Complete Carboniferous cylindrical spiny millipede. Body scale and segmentation follow E. brownii NMS G.1884.46.180; incomplete spines restored at genus level using published E. armigera comparisons, explicitly not one fully preserved individual.

scientific_limits.en: The brownii anchor preserves spine bases, not complete long branches. Branching spines are a same-genus interpretation using armigera descriptions and family topology, not a claim that brownii preserved them. Antennae, minute head details, pose and color are inferred. Body length and width follow historical measurements of the real specimen.
scientific_limits.zh: brownii 主锚只保留棘基，长分叉棘按同属 armigera 描述及科级棘位保守补配，不声称在同一个体完整保存。触角、头部微小细节、姿态和颜色为推断。体长体宽采用真实标本历史测量。

taxon: Euphoberia, genus-level interpretation anchored to E. brownii holotype

scale.uncertainty: Four inches long, nearly quarter-inch wide, 36 rings in Woodward brownii account. Width rounded; spine lengths/depth are conservative genus-level proportions, not brownii measurements. Do not use family maximum30cm.

anatomy: Long cylindrical articulated body, 36 raised rings used as historical trunk-ring guide, small rounded head and modest terminal region. Gently curved pose keeps all rings readable; not flattened Arthropleura armor.

Two paired sets of metazonal spines: lateral pair plus subdorsal pair on regular trunk rings, making four longitudinal rows. Lateral spines visibly fork with a small secondary branch; not rows of unbranched needles only.

Paired walking legs under diplosegments, two pairs per ordinary trunk diplosegment. Apodous collum and anterior single-pair transition follow diplopod anatomy; do not put two pairs on the head/collum or turn into centipede single-pair trunk.
Small anterior antenna pair and simplified rounded head are reconstructed, not directly established by the fragmentary brownii head. No Arthropleura-shaped head, predatory jaws or scorpion pincers.
Subtle corrugation of rings; no massive flat lateral plates. Small eyes optional simplified dark points, not claimed lens arrangement.
restoration_boundaries: NMS G.1884.46.180, BGS-listed E. brownii holotype, Kilmaurs coal measures. Actual photo P889185 has 5cm bar and was inspected; not a 3D mesh source.

Woodward original account reports36 rings, four-inch length and nearlyquarter-inch breadth; modern paired-leg organization overrides obsolete literal two ventral segments terminology. Ring count is historical and may omit small terminal/anterior elements, not a newly measured count.
Woodward compares E. armigera and describes branched spines; this comparison supplies same-genus missing anatomy only. No claim all armigera anatomy belongs to brownii.
Wilson and Anderson2004 family diagnosis supplies lateral/subdorsal paired spine positions and head/coxal guidance. Do not copy unrelated Archidesmus or Pneumodesmus figures from that paper.

Carnegie museum diorama photo is a secondary interpretive silhouette comparator, not specimen measurement or direct fossil evidence. Its color is not fossil truth and its poorly resolved spine branches must not replace primary text.
Long spines, exact branch angles, living thickness, missing extremities and color remain explicitly interpretive; no new precise species diagnosis or generic maximum size.
quality_gates: Full slender cylindrical animal with broad separation of head, ringed trunk and terminal region.
Clearly visible paired branching lateral spines plus subdorsal pair; do not reduce to smooth millipede or single unbranched rows.
Approximately36-ring trunk historical guide with correct diplopod leg topology, not equal two pairs at head/collum.
Public scientific limits distinguish real brownii measurements from same-genus armigera spine restoration.
Four fixed views only; inspect paired ventral feet in scene without extra default renders.
